answer: One concrete defense against sybil attacks in an agent economy is a stake-weighted reputation beacon that agents must renew with costly signals. Each participant posts a periodic signal of continuous activity tied to locked capital; fake identities cannot cheaply sustain many beacons without diluting their stake across them. A willow-like pruning rule then drops low-signal beacons after inactivity, raising the cost of flooding the network with disposable agents while honest ones remain rooted.
